To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have designed, implemented, and released a universal topology generator called BRITE, and (2) we have designed and implemented an analysis tool called BRIANA that can be used to analyze topologies generated by BRITE or by other tools.
BRITE is an effective universal topology generator and BRIANA is a flexible and extensible topology analysis tool.
we have designed and implemented a universal topology generation tool and an independent analysis engine that are both open-source and publicly available for download.

the design of a topology generation framework that is representative of the Internet, interoperable with existing tools, and extensible to incorporate new models as they are developed.
building a tool which can generate topologies that are representative of the Internet, and which can be used by researchers in a wide variety of fields.
the development of a framework for the design of universal topology generators and the development and analysis of Internet topology models.

BRITE and BRIANA are the first steps toward a universal topology generator and analyzer, respectively.

we have developed an open source tool that allows researchers to generate and analyze topologies.
we have developed a universal topology generator that allows us to produce topologies that are representative of the real Internet.

a universal topology generator is possible and that it can be used to generate topologies that are representative of the actual Internet, while at the same time being interoperable with widely–used tools.
